title: Add ./build to .gitignore
description:
The wiki instructions for [building `wireshark` on `macOS` specify to
create a `./build`
directory](https://gitlab.com/wireshark/wireshark/-/wikis/BuildingAndInstalling#macos):
```
mkdir build && cd build && cmake ../ && make
```

So this commit adds this directory to `.gitignore` to prevent
accidentally committing build artifacts.

notes.body: I was a little surprised this wasn't already part of `.gitignore`... is the omission an accident or a conscious choice? If a choice, then it might be useful to update the wiki to clarify.
it is a choice, you can have your own gitignore (and yes may be add to wiki)

Can you provide a scenario where you would want to add something from `./build` to the wireshark repository?

I'm not talking about custom forks (where someone may want custom behavior and hence a custom `.gitignore`), but rather the mainline wireshark repo... consider the long-term pain of someone accidentally committing something from `./build`, meaning even though it gets removed in a later commit it's still sitting in the git history... and those artifacts could be quite large. So wouldn't you want to protect against this...? Or is there something I'm misunderstanding?

That's not the point actually. Adding `build` to gitignore would be useless for many people including me. I don't have `build` but instead `build-foo`, `build-bar`, `build-blabla`. Despite reported in the manual, it is not hardcoded, hence it is rather pointless adding it to gitignore.

Would `*build/` and `build*/` work? As Dario points out, people might have multiple build directories. I tend to use `build` or `cmbuild`, the latter being out of habit from porting our build system to CMake.
I upvote this solution. I recall I discussed earlier with someone (maybe @Lekensteyn?) that was opposed to that, but I think it would work.

There is already `cmake-build-*` for the Jetbrains IDE (see git logs). I usually have a separate directory outside the source tree (in `/tmp/`), but `build` seems common enough to have in the .gitignore file I guess.

A pattern like `/*build*/` would catch all of `cmake-build-*`, `cmbuild`, `build`, `build2`, etc. The trailing slash would be required since otherwise it would catch `vagrant_build.sh` too. The trailing slash ensures that any deeper subdirectory with `build` in its name will not be ignored. Just in case someone tries to add it in the future.

I might have objected to it in the past, but don't mind having it now if it makes people's live easier.

> The **trailing** slash ensures that any deeper subdirectory with `build` in its name will not be ignored.

@Lekensteyn I assume you mean the "**leading**" slash? IIUC, the trailing slash indicates it's a directory, the leading slash indicates it's relative to the the root of the git repo. Please correct me if I am assuming wrongly here and you actually meant the trailing slash...
Nope, trailing, but it looks like you discovered that already:)

Note to myself: https://gitlab.com/wireshark/wireshark/-/wikis/BuildingAndInstalling#macos says after build to execute `./build/run/qtshark` but that doesn't actually exist... looks like it's actually `./build/run/wireshark`... 

I requested wiki edit permissions and will update once I get them (but if you see this and have wiki permissions yourself, feel free to update!).

I was given wiki editor permisions, but for some reason I'm still unable to edit the above-mentioned wiki page. @geraldcombs any idea what might be amiss? I saw a note about gitlab permissions required for wiki editing allow a lot of other things that aren't a good idea from a security perspective and so there were two separate groups/repos... Is that the issue here?

GitLab doesn't have separate ["developer" and "wiki editor"](https://docs.gitlab.com/ee/user/permissions.html) permissions, so we have a separate project at
https://gitlab.com/wireshark/editor-wiki/
which is editable by the "Wiki Editors" group and which syncs with the main wiki.
Thank you, I fixed it in https://gitlab.com/wireshark/editor-wiki/-/wikis/BuildingAndInstalling/diff?version_id=47b92b7c0798748de12df6e69832685a0b3070bb

Based on the feedback, I amended the commit to add `/*build*/`... The commit description is also updating to specify why the leading slash, wildcards, and trailing slash are all necessary. H/T to @Lekensteyn for pointing out the value of the leading slash.

Thoughts?

FWIW, the Windows build steps in the Developers Guide have always shown an out of tree build, in a directory that is a sibling of the sources, see https://www.wireshark.org/docs/wsdg_html_chunked/ChSetupWin32.html#ChSetupPrepareCommandCom

Ideally I would expect all platforms to use the same procedure, personally I prefer an out of tree build, I think it's easier to recover from "issues" and less likely to mess up your local git repo if you do make a mistake as has been often seen over the years when supporting new folks to get their dev. env. setup.

> personally I prefer an out of tree build, I think it's easier to recover from "issues" and less likely to mess up your local git repo if you do make a mistake as has been often seen over the years when supporting new folks to get their dev. env. setup.

I could certainly support that. I think the only thing I'm trying to avoid is n00bs coming in, reading "use `./build` and then accidentally committing some files with a `git add *` and then trying to cleanup their mess. We should make it easier for them to avoid this... either with a `.gitignore` addition, or by avoiding suggesting building within the repo directory structure...

Although I do wonder... do we lose anything with `/*build*/` in `.gitignore?` I think that at worst it'd be simply harmless, and at best it'd prevent the aforementioned issues.

commits_data.title: Add /*build*/ to .gitignore
commits_data.message:
Add /*build*/ to .gitignore

A common pattern is to build the source artifacts within a *build* dir.

For example, the wiki instructions for [building `wireshark` on `macOS` specify to
create a `./build`
directory](https://gitlab.com/wireshark/wireshark/-/wikis/BuildingAndInstalling#macos):
```
mkdir build && cd build && cmake ../ && make
```

So this commit adds this directory to `.gitignore` to prevent
accidentally committing build artifacts.

The specific format `/*build*/` protects against the following:
1. The leading slash makes sure only top-level directories that match
this pattern are ignored.
2. The trailing slash makes sure that only directories (and not files)
are ignored.
3. The wildcards catch all the various variations on `build` folder name
that are used...
